newsitem.title: UK: LME copper spins wheels, finishes just easier.
newsitem.headline: LME copper spins wheels, finishes just easier.

text.p: Lacklustre base metals spent the afternoon meandering in narrow price ranges on Wednesday, with flagship copper consolidating amid unimpressive volumes.
Zinc was the best performer in the complex, touching the $1,340 resistance level on general speculative buying in the afternoon kerb for the second time this week.
Three months zinc finished $2 firmer at $1,339 per tonne.
"Zinc is eroding resistance slowly but surely. Once it closes above $1,340 the next move is $1,400," a trader said.
Copper, by contrast, wrapped up the day $3 easier at $2,414, after failing to regain early highs.
Copper prices had initially pushed higher on short covering sparked by a 2,825-tonne LME stock decline.
But the pre-market gains faded amid commission house selling and liquidation and never returned.
"The market picked up early but never was able to follow through into a rally. Copper is consolidating its recent gains before resuming to move higher," a trader said.
"Volumes were very light all day -- a waste of everyone's time."
Still, analysts and dealers said copper was still on target to conquer the $2,440 resistance level, the high of the year, in coming days.
The cash to threes backwardation moved in tandem with three months prices, easing to $53/$57, versus $55/$60.
The other metals were little changed to softer.
Aluminium crumpled towards the $1,650 support level on disappointed liquidation after failing in recent days to breach tough support above $1,670.
Traders said it could still ease further towards $1,640 before trying the upside again.
Tin was $5 firmer at $5,730, suggesting that prices were stabilising after recent bouts of producer sales bullied the market, traders said.
Nickel, however was $40 lower at $7,730 after general liquidation took its toll.
Lead was unchanged at $622 after bouncing off early lows touched when fund sales triggered sell stops and pushed prices to a low of $615.
"Tin, lead and nickel are weary. They're still struggling before any buying is going to come in," a trader said.
Alloy was last indicated little changed at $1,515/$1,520.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
